extraction_scope: 23 key geographic locations from PKD's life, novels, and short stories. Includes biographical residences, novel settings, and places mentioned in works.

works: The Man in the High Castle

explicit_topics: Literary locations from novels (UBIK, Scanner Darkly, Man in the High Castle, VALIS)
Biographical events tied to places (Point Reyes idyll, Orange County crisis, etc.)

claims_made_by_source.claim: PKD was born in Chicago on December 16, 1928 at 7812 Emerald Avenue
PKD's family moved to San Francisco Bay Area in late 1929, beginning lifelong California residence
Berkeley was PKD's formative residence from 1931 through adolescence and early adulthood
PKD and wife Kleo moved to Point Reyes Station in September 1958 for idyllic retreat and creative work
Orange County became site of PKD's recovery from drug culture (1972-1974) and later psychiatric crisis (1976)
UBIK novel set in 1992 with primary locations in New York City and Green River, Utah
A Scanner Darkly set in Orange County, California 1994 with multiple Anaheim, Long Beach, Santa Ana locations
The Man in the High Castle set in alternate-history post-WWII America with San Francisco and western zones under Japanese control

important_passages.excerpt: PKD was born December 16, 1928 at 7812 Emerald Avenue in Chicago
important_passages.why_important: Establishes birthplace and date; twin sister Jane died here on January 26, 1929, shaping PKD's entire life

important_passages.excerpt: Point Reyes Station: house on corner of Mariana and Lorraine with caboose in backyard used as writing studio
important_passages.why_important: Idyllic creative space representing PKD's aspirations for stable, productive life

uncertainties: Exact addresses for some Berkeley residences incomplete
Specific dates of some moves approximate rather than exact
Novel settings may contain fictional elements beyond geographic setting
Some locations mentioned only tangentially in sources
